court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
trial_court: S.B. Jalna Police Station, Jalna for the offence punishable under Sections 498-A, 323 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code
case_name: Nitin S/O. Motilal Patte And Anr vs The State Of Maharashtra And Anr

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Nitin S/o Motilal Patte, Manisha W/o Nitin Patte
parties.respondent_defendant: The State of Maharashtra, Manisha W/o Sachin Patte

facts_of_case: Accused persons filed applications to quash proceedings arising out of matrimonial dispute. Parties settled their dispute amicably and informant does not want to prosecute matter.

legal_principles.principle: The court may exercise its inherent powers to quash proceedings if the parties have settled their dispute amicably.
legal_principles.held: Since the First Information Report as well as the CRIA1561.19 proceedings were arising out of the matrimonial dispute and the husband and the wife have settled their dispute amicably, case is made out for exercise of inherent powers of this Court under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the court to exercise its inherent powers judiciously and not arbitrarily.

outcome.final_order: Criminal Application No.1561 of 2019 and Criminal Application No.2336 of 2022 stand allowed. First Information Report vide Crime No.190 of 2019 registered with S.B. Jalna Police Station, Jalna for the offence punishable under Sections 498-A, 323 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code and the proceedings before the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Jalna, arising out of the said First Information Report, bearing Criminal M.A. No.922 of 2020, stand quashed and set aside as against the accused persons.

keywords: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
